answer.why: It sounds like the goal is right there in the title: climb up and get rich and powerful, which is exactly the kind of ambitious, slightly cheeky life I like in BitLife-style games. It's short, punchy and made me curious how much a minister actually earns.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical, ambitious climb-the-ladder game where the big payoff is becoming a minister and seeing a huge pay packet, with money, politics, scandals and choices that come back to bite me. I'd guess it's about chasing power and cash, possibly a bit tongue-in-cheek.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: No idea, honestly. It sounds like dry legal or HR jargon, maybe a game about job contracts or paperwork, or something to do with religion or a medical-style term. I wouldn't guess it was a fun life sim and would probably scroll straight past.

best_moment.what: Writing down what everyone was really thinking at the Public Sector Transformation offsite. It felt like a bold, dramatic choice, though I never saw it pay off.

worst_moment.what: The BTO flat year. I had no idea what BTO meant, so I picked the 'inside info' option blind and the game never explained it.

skip_year.why: There were only two years, so nothing was long enough to skip. The ending card was the flattest part, but it isn't a year.

answer.held_back_by: My guess is the favour I asked in Y1 and the blunt offsite note in Y2 together. But the ending says the scholarship mattered and my file didn't ever put a ceiling on me, which I didn't understand. I never had a scholarship, so it feels like something was decided before I started.
answer.ending_fair_why: It ended at 24 after two taps, with no warning and no chance to recover. The card hints at a scholarship I never knew about, so I can't tell what I did wrong. A shock exit is fine in a game like this, but I'd want to understand why it happened.
answer.chase_next: I'd go for the top: get invited into politics and see how far up I can climb. I'd play it straight this time to find out what the game does with a clean run.
answer.play_again_why: Yes, mostly because it was over so quickly and I want to see what happens past year 2. I'm also curious what the scholarship thing means and whether the game has more to it than this.

tone_breaks.line: That is what the scholarship was for.
tone_breaks.note: I never saw a scholarship in my run, so this line assumes something I wasn't told. It reads as a dig at the system, which is fine, but it confused me.

tone_breaks.line: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
tone_breaks.note: Slightly knowing and smirky. It's funny, but it nudges me to see the game as being clever instead of just telling me what happened.

answer.title_fit_why: I never got near a minister's salary, so that title didn't fit my run. The other one sounds like the civil service jargon the game kept using, and it suggests the point is surviving and being kept on, which is what I failed at.
